claims.statement: CTIS gives public users searchable trial facts and downloadable records, but the cited public fields do not establish the private operational outcomes required by the thesis.
Personal data, commercially confidential information, confidential authority communications, and supervision-sensitive material are protected from public disclosure.
Startup, recruitment, patient access, and data quality are commercially relevant performance dimensions, although published multinational evidence is limited.
The feasibility and site-selection market has strong incumbents advertising large proprietary datasets, operational performance metrics, site workflow, and integrations.
A site-controlled evidence passport may avoid the weakest generic-ranking position and offer portability that incumbent sponsor-centric products do not emphasize.
No gathered evidence establishes that Polish sites can lawfully contribute comparable outcomes, that CROs will trust them, or that either side will pay at the proposed levels.
No gathered source supplies public incumbent pricing, customer acquisition cost, implementation cost, renewal, or attainable gross-margin evidence.

contrary_evidence: Three major incumbents already market feasibility and site-performance capabilities based on proprietary operational data.
CTIS transparency is bounded by privacy and commercial-confidentiality protections and does not substitute for contribution rights.
Published research supports performance measurement, but limited external datasets and study-specific context weaken a universal reliability score.
No direct willingness-to-contribute or willingness-to-pay evidence was found.
